entity.agency: WA Secretary of State, Corporations Division
entity.summary: If you form an LLC, corporation or partnership, file it with the Secretary of State first, then apply for your state business license.
entity.quote: If your business structure will be one of the following, you must file with the Washington Secretary of State before filing the Business License Application

state_tax.agency: WA Department of Revenue (Business Licensing Service)
state_tax.summary: Apply for a Washington business license with the Department of Revenue. You get a Unified Business Identifier (UBI) number, which you need before contractor registration.
state_tax.quote: When you receive your business license, you’ll be assigned a Unified Business Identifier (UBI) number. This number is unique to your business, and you’ll need it whenever you file your taxes or make changes to your business.

unemployment.summary: When you hire employees, add hiring to your Department of Revenue business license application; that registers you for unemployment insurance taxes with ESD.
unemployment.quote: If you have employees in Washington, you need to apply for a license from the state Department of Revenue .

workers_comp.summary: Washington employers buy workers' comp from L&I (the state fund). Business owners (sole proprietors), exempt corporate officers and partners are not required to cover themselves, but can elect coverage.
workers_comp.quote: No. Owners of businesses (sole proprietors), exempt corporate officers, and partners aren't required to have workers' comp coverage in this state.

local.summary: Some cities and counties require their own business license endorsements, added through your state business license application.
local.quote: Your business requires city endorsements , county endorsements , and state endorsements .

residential_building.name: Construction Contractor Registration (General or Specialty)
residential_building.covers: All construction contractors, residential or commercial: building, remodeling, repairing and demolishing. General contractors can do most work and hire subs; specialty contractors work only in their specialty.
prerequisites: Register your business with the Department of Revenue (UBI number)
Continuous contractor surety bond ($30,000 general / $15,000 specialty) or assignment of savings
General liability insurance ($200,000 public liability and $50,000 property damage, or $250,000 combined single limit)
Notarized Application for Contractor Registration
residential_building.bond: $30,000 surety bond for general contractors, $15,000 for specialty contractors (or an assigned savings account).
residential_building.insurance: General liability: $200,000 public liability and $50,000 property damage, or $250,000 combined single limit, with L&I listed as certificate holder.
residential_building.summary: Washington requires all construction contractors to register with L&I before bidding, advertising or working. You need a UBI number, a surety bond and general liability insurance. You must show your registration number in all ads and bids.
residential_building.quote: Washington State requires all construction contractors to register with L&I. State law also requires construction contractors to be bonded and insured to protect the public.
residential_building.note: A Model Disclosure Statement must be given to customers on residential jobs of $1,000 or more.

evidence.quote: Register your business with Department of Revenue . Get a surety bond or an assignment of savings. Purchase a general liability insurance policy. Complete your Application for Contractor Registration.
$30,000 for general contractors. $15,000 for specialty contractors.
$200,000 in public liability and $50,000 property damage, or $250,000 combined single limit.
An original, completed Application for Contractor Registration (F625-001-000) with notarized signatures

commercial_building.name: Construction Contractor Registration (General or Specialty)
commercial_building.covers: Same registration as residential work; it covers buildings, roads and other real property.
prerequisites: UBI number from the Department of Revenue
Contractor surety bond or assignment of savings
General liability insurance
commercial_building.bond: Same bond as residential (general or specialty amount).
commercial_building.insurance: Same general liability insurance as residential.
commercial_building.summary: There is no separate commercial license. The same L&I contractor registration covers commercial and residential construction work.
commercial_building.quote: Once registered, contractors can bid, advertise, and perform construction work. This can include constructing, remodeling, repairing and demolishing buildings, roads and other real property.

evidence.quote: Register your business with Department of Revenue . Get a surety bond or an assignment of savings. Purchase a general liability insurance policy.

electrical.name: Electrical Contractor License; Electrician (journey level/specialty), Master Electrician and Electrical Administrator certificates
electrical.agency: WA Department of Labor & Industries, Electrical Program
electrical.covers: Any business doing electrical work needs an electrical contractor license; anyone doing the work needs an electrician or trainee certificate.
prerequisites: Valid UBI number
$4,000 electrical contractor bond or assignment of savings
A designated master electrician or electrical administrator (who must pass a qualifying exam)
Electricians: required experience and education, then pass the exam (start as a trainee)
electrical.bond: $4,000 electrical/telecommunications contractor bond or assignment of savings.
electrical.summary: To do electrical work as a business you need an L&I electrical contractor license with a UBI number, a bond and an assigned master electrician or administrator. Individuals start as trainees and must have experience and pass an exam to become certified electricians.
electrical.quote: To do electrical work, you must get an electrical contractor license from us. You must have a valid UBI number, either a $4,000 bond or assignment of savings, and a designated master electrician or administrator.

evidence.quote: To become an electrical administrator , you must pass a qualifying exam.
To become a certified general journey level or specialty electrician , you must have the required experience and education and pass the appropriate exam.

plumbing.name: Plumber Certification (journey level PL01, residential PL02, residential service PL04, others)
plumbing.agency: WA Department of Labor & Industries, Plumber Certification Program
plumbing.covers: Anyone working in the plumbing trade must be certified. Plumbing businesses register as contractors with L&I.
prerequisites: Start as a plumber trainee
Journey level: four years (at least 8,000 hours) as a supervised trainee
Residential: 3 years (at least 6,000 hours) in the specialty
Contractor registration with L&I for the business
plumbing.summary: Washington certifies individual plumbers; you typically begin as a trainee and log supervised hours before a journey level or specialty certificate. A plumbing business also needs L&I contractor registration with bond and insurance.
plumbing.quote: You must be certified by the Washington State Plumber Certification Program to work in the plumbing trade in Washington.

evidence.quote: Four years or more (at least 8,000 hours) working as a plumber trainee under the supervision of a certified journey level plumber.
3 years or more (at least 6,000 hours) working in the specialty under supervision of a certified residential or journey level plumber.
To become a certified journey level or specialty plumber in Washington, you must typically begin as a plumber trainee .
However, contractors working with plumbing , electrical , elevators , mobile home installation , boilers , and asbestos have additional requirements for education, examination, and licensing.

mechanical.name: Specialty Contractor Registration (HVAC)
mechanical.covers: HVAC is one of the L&I contractor specialties; there is no separate state HVAC/mechanical contractor license.
prerequisites: L&I contractor registration with bond and insurance
Electrical wiring on HVAC/refrigeration equipment falls under the electrical licensing rules
mechanical.insurance: General liability insurance as for all registered contractors.
mechanical.summary: HVAC contractors register with L&I as specialty contractors. Washington has no separate statewide mechanical license, but the electrical parts of HVAC work fall under L&I electrical licensing, and boilers have their own rules.
mechanical.quote: L&I regulates 63 specialties that each require contractor registration. These specialties include roofing, painting, HVAC, tree removal, mobile home set-up, and dozens more.
mechanical.note: Washington's electrical program includes HVAC/refrigeration electrical specialties; check with L&I for which certificate applies.

evidence.quote: You must have a valid electrical certificate or license from us to do electrical work in Washington.

roofing.name: Specialty Contractor Registration (Roofing)
roofing.covers: Roofing is one of the L&I specialty contractor classifications.
prerequisites: UBI number
Specialty contractor surety bond
General liability insurance
roofing.insurance: General liability insurance as for all registered contractors.
roofing.summary: Roofers register with L&I as specialty contractors (or as general contractors). There is no separate roofing license beyond registration.
roofing.quote: L&I regulates 63 specialties that each require contractor registration. These specialties include roofing, painting, HVAC, tree removal, mobile home set-up, and dozens more.

evidence.quote: $30,000 for general contractors. $15,000 for specialty contractors.

pesticide.name: Commercial Applicator License (and Structural Pest Inspector license)
pesticide.covers: Applying pesticides to someone else's property (pest control, lawn/weed control, tree spraying).
prerequisites: Pass the required WSDA pesticide exams
UBI number showing the business is registered to do business in Washington
Proof of financial responsibility (insurance)
pesticide.insurance: Proof of financial responsibility is required for the license.
pesticide.summary: Applying pesticides on other people's property requires a WSDA Commercial Applicator License, a joint company-person license held by whoever makes application decisions. You must pass exams and show a valid UBI number.
pesticide.quote: Applying pesticides to the lands/property of another requires the Commercial Applicator License. This is a joint company – person license. The person who makes the pesticide application decisions for the company must obtain the license.
pesticide.note: Insurance requirement is in RCW 17.21.160; not quoted here.

evidence.quote: The applicant must pass the required exams and furnish information that they are legal to do business in the state of Washington by supplying their UBI number

asbestos.name: Certified Asbestos Contractor; Asbestos Supervisor and Worker certificates
asbestos.covers: Removing or abating asbestos. Any contractor must also have a good faith asbestos inspection before renovation or demolition.
prerequisites: Active L&I contractor registration
A Certified Asbestos Supervisor on payroll (40-hour supervisor course)
Workers: 32-hour Asbestos Worker training course
asbestos.summary: Asbestos abatement contractors must be certified by L&I and employ a certified supervisor; workers need certification too. All contractors must have a good faith asbestos inspection done before remodeling or demolition work that could disturb suspect materials.
asbestos.quote: A good faith inspection for asbestos, performed by an AHERA certified building inspector is required before any remodel, repair, removal, or other work that could disturb suspect materials.

evidence.quote: An active Contractor Registration with the WA Dept. of Labor and Industries.
A Certified Asbestos Supervisor on your payroll.
Attend a 40-hour Asbestos Supervisor training course.
Attend a 32-hour Asbestos Worker training course.

lead_rrp.name: Renovation, Repair and Painting (RRP) certification
lead_rrp.agency: WA Department of Commerce, Lead-Based Paint Program
lead_rrp.covers: Firms and individuals who offer, bid or contract renovation work on pre-1978 homes and child-occupied facilities.
prerequisites: RRP certification from the WA Department of Commerce (state-run program)
lead_rrp.summary: Washington runs its own lead RRP program through the Department of Commerce instead of EPA. You or your company need RRP certification to work on pre-1978 homes or child-occupied facilities.
lead_rrp.quote: Commerce’s Lead-Based Paint programs protect public health by providing training, certification and compliance enforcement for lead-safe practices.

evidence.quote: You or your company need this certification if you: Offer, bid, or contract to work on pre-1978 properties

other.name: Elevator, boiler and mobile home installation licensing
other.summary: Contractors working on elevators, mobile home installation or boilers have extra education, exam and licensing requirements beyond contractor registration.
other.quote: However, contractors working with plumbing , electrical , elevators , mobile home installation , boilers , and asbestos have additional requirements for education, examination, and licensing.

other.name: Specialty Contractor Registration (tree removal)
other.summary: Tree removal is an L&I contractor specialty that requires contractor registration.
other.quote: L&I regulates 63 specialties that each require contractor registration. These specialties include roofing, painting, HVAC, tree removal, mobile home set-up, and dozens more.

other.name: Telecommunications Contractor License (low voltage)
other.summary: Telecommunications (low voltage) businesses need an L&I telecommunications contractor license with a UBI number, bond, liability insurance and a designated administrator.
other.quote: To engage in the business of doing telecommunications work, you must get a telecommunications contractor license from us.
